cards.text: Solomon is Israel's new king, and the first thing we hear is a BIG move. He forms an alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt by marrying his daughter. He brings her to the City of David while he finishes some building.

cards.question: Solomon's building list has his palace, the house of the LORD, and one more thing. What is it?

cards.text: But here's the catch. There's no house for the Name of the LORD yet, so the people are still sacrificing somewhere else.

cards.question: With no house built for the LORD's Name yet, where are the people sacrificing?

cards.text: Now, Solomon himself. He walks in the statutes of his father David, the king before him.

cards.question: True or false: Solomon loved the LORD.
Solomon walked in his father David's statutes, with one exception. What was it?

answers.text: He sacrificed on the high places

cards.text: So the king heads to Gibeon to sacrifice, because it was the great high place.

cards.question: At Gibeon, Solomon offered a ___ burnt offerings on the altar.

cards.text: A THOUSAND. Friend, I stamped forty cookies in a row once and had to go lie down on my gold base. Then one night at Gibeon, the LORD appears to Solomon in a dream.

cards.question: In the dream at Gibeon, what does God say to Solomon?

answers.text: Ask and I will give it to you
Go and build My house for Me
Rise and lead My people out

cards.text: Before Solomon asks for anything, he looks back at his father David. He says God showed David much loving devotion.

cards.question: Why does Solomon say God showed his father David so much loving devotion?

answers.text: David won every battle he fought

cards.text: And God kept that devotion going by giving David a son to sit on his throne this very day. That son is Solomon, made king in his father's place.

cards.question: Solomon is king now. How does he describe himself to God?

cards.text: A brand-new king, and he says he doesn't know how to go out or come in. That's day one as the BOSS, holding the keys to the whole building, and you can't even find the light switch.

cards.question: Solomon says he's among the people God has chosen. True or false: he says they're too numerous to count or number.
So God said ask. What does Solomon ask God to give him?
Solomon wants to judge God's people and discern between good and evil. Why does he say he needs help?

answers.text: No one is able to govern them
The people refuse to obey him

cards.text: Now it pleased the Lord that Solomon asked for this. Me? I'd have asked for an oven that never burns a batch, and called it a prayer request.
So God answers him, starting with what Solomon DIDN'T ask for. Not long life, and not wealth for himself.

cards.question: Besides long life and wealth, what else does God say Solomon didn't ask for?
God says He'll do what Solomon asked and give him a wise and ___ heart.
True or false: God says there will never have been another like Solomon, and there never will be.

cards.text: Then God keeps going. He's about to give Solomon something he never requested.

cards.question: What does God give Solomon on top of what he asked for?

cards.text: Riches AND honor, with no man in any kingdom his equal all his days. That's like asking for one cookie and walking out with the bakery, the ovens AND the delivery cart.

cards.question: God adds one promise with an if. If Solomon walks in God's ways like David did, what will God do?

cards.text: Then Solomon wakes up, and sure enough, it had been a dream. The best dream I ever had was a cookie box that packed itself, and I woke up hugging my own mustache.

cards.question: Solomon wakes up at Gibeon. Where does he go next?

cards.text: In Jerusalem, Solomon stands before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. He offers burnt offerings and peace offerings.

cards.question: After his offerings before the ark, how does Solomon wrap it all up?

answers.text: He holds a feast for his servants
He builds a new altar at Gibeon
He writes a song for the people

findings.problem: The card calls Solomon 'Israel's new king,' but 1 Kings 3:1 doesn't say that. It comes from 3:7 or from outside the passage (1 Kings 2:12). The card cites only 1 Kings 3:1, so the citation is narrower than what the card uses.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card introduces David as 'the king before him.' That fact comes from 1 Kings 3:6-7 ('made Your servant king in my father David's place'), but the card cites only 1 Kings 3:3.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'A THOUSAND.', the forty-cookies joke, and the dream at Gibeon. It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The blank asks for the number of burnt offerings (thousand, hundred or dozen). No earlier card gives anything to reason from, so the baker is guessing wording they haven't seen.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Most choice cards in this stop can only be answered by luck. Card 2 (the wall around Jerusalem), card 4 (the high places), card 9 (a thousand), card 11 (Ask and I will give it to you), card 15 (only a little child) and card 17 (too numerous to count) all come with no reasoning clues in the setup. That is 6 of 11 choice cards, so discovery questions are the majority instead of a few.

rule.text: A few discovery questions are fine. Some moments can't be reasoned out, like where Jonah's ship is headed. A few of those are okay, as long as most choice cards are informed guesses.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. 8 of 11 choice cards are multiple choice, 2 are true or false and 1 is fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop. 5 of 7 choice cards are multiple choice, 1 is true or false and 1 is fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: The answers don't share a tone. 'Riches to build Your house' speaks to God in Solomon's own voice ('Your'). The right answer and the other wrong answer are neutral descriptions. The right answer, 'An understanding heart,' also sounds more like the Bible than 'Strength to win every war.'

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answers 'The city of Gezer' and 'The city of Megiddo' are false in 1 Kings 3:1-15. But Solomon does build both later (1 Kings 9:15-17), and Gezer is the dowry Pharaoh gives his daughter, Solomon's wife (1 Kings 9:16). A baker who knows this could argue those answers are right. Stop 2, card 7 has the same issue: 'Peace and rest' is something God gives Solomon in 1 Kings 5:4.
findings.question: The rules require wrong answers to be false anywhere in the passage, and they encourage real details from elsewhere in the Bible. Should a wrong answer also be ruled out when it is true of the same person somewhere else in Scripture?
